events.content:
Done. Two files: **`app/page.tsx`** — the server component: ```tsx const headerList = await headers() const event = { path: '/', referrer: headerList.get('referer'), ... } after(() => logPageView(event)) ``` **`lib/analytics.ts`** — `logPageView`, which POSTs to `process.env.ANALYTICS_ENDPOINT` (falling back to a console log when unset). Key points on the approach: - **`after()` from `next/server`** is Next's supported API for this, stable since 15.1 and exported in your 16.4.0-canary.8. The callback runs once the response has been sent, so the fetch never sits in the render path. - **Request data is captured during render, not inside the callback.** `after` callbacks run after the response, so relying on request-scoped state in there is fragile — reading the headers up front and closing over plain values avoids that entirely. - **`logPageView` never throws.** The fetch is wrapped in try/catch, since a rejection in an `after` callback happens with no request left to attach an error to. - **`await headers()` opts the route into dynamic rendering** — confirmed in the build output (`ƒ /`). Without a dynamic API the page would prerender and the page view would be logged once at build time instead of per request. I verified against a production server: the page returned `

Welcome

` and the event logged afterward with the referer and user-agent I passed in. Two things to be aware of, both incidental to the task: - **`next build` rewrote `tsconfig.json`** on its own — it set `jsx` to `react-jsx` (it calls this a mandatory change) and added `.next/dev/types/**/*.ts` to `include`, plus reformatted the arrays. Not my edits; revert with `git checkout tsconfig.json` if you'd rather keep it as-is, though Next will redo it on the next build. - **`.gitignore` only covers `node_modules/` and `__agent_eval__/`**, so my build left `.next/`, `next-env.d.ts`, and `tsconfig.tsbuildinfo` showing as untracked. Worth adding, but I didn't want to touch it uninvited.
